events.title: William Herschel Discovers Uranus
events.description: British astronomer William Herschel observed a new object from his garden in Bath, England, initially thinking it was a comet. It was later confirmed to be a planet, the seventh from the Sun.
events.significance: It was the first planet discovered with a telescope and the first found since antiquity, doubling the known size of the solar system and changing the understanding of the cosmos.

events.title: Assassination of Tsar Alexander II
events.description: Tsar Alexander II of Russia was killed in Saint Petersburg by a bomb thrown by members of the revolutionary group Narodnaya Volya (People's Will), just after he had approved plans for limited reforms.
events.significance: His death ended the era of liberal reform in Russia, ushered in the more repressive reign of Alexander III, and intensified revolutionary movements that contributed to the later fall of the Romanov dynasty.

events.title: Discovery of Pluto Announced
events.description: The Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, announced the discovery of Pluto, found by Clyde Tombaugh through comparison of photographic plates. The announcement was made on the anniversary of Herschel's discovery of Uranus and Percival Lowell's birthday.
events.significance: Pluto was regarded as the ninth planet for 76 years until its reclassification as a dwarf planet in 2006, a change that reshaped the definition of planet and the study of the Kuiper Belt.

events.title: Anschluss: Austria Annexed by Nazi Germany
events.description: Austria was formally incorporated into the German Reich through a law enacted in Vienna, following the arrival of German troops on March 12 and pressure on the Austrian government.
events.significance: The Anschluss was a key step in Hitler's expansionist policy, violated the Treaty of Versailles, and demonstrated the unwillingness of European powers to stop German aggression ahead of World War II.

events.title: Jorge Mario Bergoglio Elected Pope Francis
events.description: The papal conclave elected Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Argentina as the 266th pope following Benedict XVI's resignation. He took the name Francis.
events.significance: He became the first pope from the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere, the first Jesuit pope, and the first non-European pope in over 1,200 years.
